chunks: From him, from Al-Qasim al-Zayyat, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Musa ibn al-A'ala, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When the water laid bare the bones of the dead, Noah (peace be upon him) saw that and panicked with an intense panic, and was aggrieved due to that.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Revealed unto him: 'This is your doing, you supplicated against them'.
So he said: 'O Lord! I seek Forgiveness from You and I repent to You'.
So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Revealed unto him: 'If you were to eat the black grapes, it would do away with (remove) your grief'.
ai.seo_question: What caused Noah's intense grief after the flood and how did Allah comfort him?
ai.summary: In this narrative from *Al-Kafi*, Prophet Noah’s profound grief upon seeing the exposed bones of his people is attributed to the weight of his own supplication for their destruction, highlighting the power of divine words in Shia theology. Upon his repentance, Allah instructs him to eat black grapes as a specific remedy to alleviate his sorrow, linking physical sustenance with spiritual healing. This event is cited in Chapter 98 to establish the prophetic precedent and merit of consuming black grapes, a practice highly recommended in Shia tradition for health and well-being.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Al Qasin Al Zayyat, from Aban Bin Usman, from Musa Bin Al A’ala, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘When the water laid bare the bones of the dead, so Noah<sup>as</sup> saw that and panicked with an intense panic, and was aggrieved due to that.
So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “This is your doing, you<sup>as</sup> supplicated against them”.
So he<sup>as</sup> said: ‘O Lord<sup>azwj</sup>! I<sup>as</sup> seek Forgiveness from You<sup>azwj</sup> and I<sup>as</sup> repent to You<sup>azwj</sup>’.
So Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Revealed unto him<sup>as</sup>: “If you<sup>as</sup> were to eat the black grapes, it would do away with (remove) your grief’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from al-Qasim al-Zayyat from Aban ibn ‘Uthman from Musa ibn al-‘Ala’ who has said the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
When water dried up and bones of the dead bodies were unveiled, Nuh, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, became extremely unhappy and sad.
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent him revelation that said, ‘This is your own act. It was you who prayed against them.’
Nuh said, ‘My Lord, I ask You to forgive me and I turn to You (for kindness).’
Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent him revelation to eat black grapes.’”
